signals.signal: Own-locator census taken 27/08/2026 (Drupal view sucursale_cec_bank, all-localities query, de-duplicated on name+address) returns 2,511 distinct locations: 1,244 ATMs, 256 MFMs (multifunction machines, i.e. cash-in capable), 963 agentii and 48 sucursale. The 963+48 = 1,011 territorial units reconciles EXACTLY with the Pillar 3 disclosure figure of 1,011 territorial units at 31/12/2025, which validates the de-duplication method. Machines total 1,500 vs the 1,484 disclosed at 31/12/2025 (1,220 ATMs + 264 MFMs): ATMs +24, MFMs -8. Deposit-capable share of the estate is 256/1,500 = 17.1%.
signals.source_name: CEC Bank branch/ATM locator (cec.ro/sucursale, all-localities query)
signals.implies: Two hard facts for Printec. (a) The branch network has NOT shrunk - 1,011 units at 31/12/2025 and 1,011 today - so the Podaru 'we will not close agencies' statement is now empirically confirmed eight months on; the addressable base for in-branch recyclers and self-service zones is intact at four figures. (b) The cash-in gap has WIDENED, not closed: MFMs fell by 8 while ATMs rose by 24, so 83% of the estate is still cash-out-only. That is a ~1,244-unit recycler/deposit-module replacement white space at Romania's #3 device operator.
signals.likelihood: Certain as a measurement; the refresh decision is the variable
signals.followup: Re-run this locator query monthly - it is a clean, machine-readable estate tracker. Ask CEC why MFM count fell 264->256 (decommissioning of early units would signal a refresh wave starting).

signals.signal: On 04/08/2026 CEC Bank launched 'Cash2Card', letting anyone - including non-customers - deposit cash directly onto any Visa or Mastercard DEBIT card issued by any bank in Romania, free of charge, in real time, 24/7, through CEC Bank's multifunction ATMs (MFMs). The bank states it has 'peste 270 de aparate MFM, toate de ultima generatie' (over 270 MFMs, all latest-generation). Quote attributed to Mihaela Bujac, Deputy Director, Cards Directorate. Page last modified 13/08/2026. NOTE: the bank's own locator returned only 256 MFM locations on 27/08/2026, so the 'over 270' claim is 14+ machines ahead of the published locator - one of the two figures is stale.
signals.source_name: CEC Bank press release 'CEC Bank lanseaza serviciul Cash2Card' + CEC Bank product page 'Depunere instant numerar pe card'
signals.implies: CEC is deliberately monetising its cash-in estate as shared national infrastructure - opening MFMs to other banks' cardholders for free to win footfall and interchange/scheme economics. This transforms the business case for deposit-capable hardware: every extra MFM now serves the whole Romanian card base, not just CEC's customers, which is exactly the argument that justifies a large recycler rollout. Direct opening for cash recyclers, cash automation and the card-scheme-certified deposit application; also raises cash-handling, CIT and reconciliation volumes, i.e. managed services.
signals.likelihood: High that MFM deployment accelerates within 6-12 months - the bank has just made deposit capability a public commitment
signals.followup: Ask the Cards Directorate (Mihaela Bujac) for the Cash2Card volume ramp and the MFM deployment plan behind 'over 270'. Establish whether the 256 MFMs are true recyclers (cash re-dispensed) or deposit-only - Cash2Card economics push strongly toward recycling.

signals.signal: The 'Agentia Digitala' product page (last modified 31/07/2026, re-checked 27/08/2026) still lists exactly FIVE Digital Agencies - Simeria (Hunedoara), Tibanesti (Iasi), Mioveni (Arges), Jurilovca (Tulcea), Floresti (Cluj) - i.e. no sixth site has opened in the ~12 weeks since the 05/06/2026 pilot launch. The page describes the format as 24/7 self-service equipment covering cash withdrawals AND cash deposits, FX, payments, transfers and personal-data updates, plus video/telephone-assisted support for account opening, lending and electronic document signing.
signals.implies: The pilot-to-rollout decision has NOT yet been taken - the window to influence the equipment specification is still open. A sixth address appearing on this page remains the single cleanest rollout trigger to monitor at this bank. The published spec (cash in + cash out + FX + payments in one unattended lobby, with videobanking) is a recycler + FX kiosk + videobanking-pod specification.
signals.likelihood: Medium - extension is committed in principle but still has no published number or date
signals.followup: Poll this page monthly. Time an approach to the post-pilot review with a per-site TCO for recycler + FX kiosk + videobanking pod.

signals.signal: CEC Bank's FY2025 Investor Presentation ('Performance Review & Strategic Priorities', posted to the IR site June 2026 - a document the previous run never saw) discloses for the first time the physical-format counts behind the strategy: '24/7 self-service zones (46 units)', 'cashless units (5)', 'Mortgage Shop (5 units)' and AgriCEC locations, under the strategic pillar 'Enhanced customer experience'. The same slide states 'Branches remain central on medium term, complemented by MB, IB, Call Centre and SoftPOS merchant terminals'.
signals.source_name: CEC Bank - Investor Presentation, Year-end results 2025 (PDF, slides 'Main strategic pillars' / 'End-to-end transformation since 2020')
signals.implies: This is the missing denominator. Only 46 of 1,011 territorial units (4.5%) currently have a 24/7 self-service zone, and only 5 are cashless. Management has committed publicly to converting rather than closing units, so the gap between 46 and 1,011 is the explicit, quantified pipeline for self-service zones, recyclers and in-lobby kiosks - the largest single addressable number found at this bank. 'Cashless units (5)' also shows the bank is willing to run branches with no manned cash desk, which is precisely the format that requires a recycler.
signals.likelihood: High - the concept is already proven in 46 sites and is named as a strategic pillar
signals.followup: Ask CEC for the annual conversion run-rate of 24/7 self-service zones (46 today - what was it a year ago?) and the standard equipment bill of materials per zone. That run-rate times the per-zone TCO is the deal size.

signals.signal: The FY2025 Investor Presentation gives the first public status on the Temenos core-banking replacement beyond generic wording: 'Core Banking System (pilot launched, migration in progress)'. It also names, for the first time in an IR document, the wider systems stack being replaced: 'Core Banking System, FIS Quantum & Pluridio (modern treasury platform), ERP (updated financial-accounting platform), CRM'. Separately the presentation discloses that in 2025 'more than 92% of investments [were] linked to IT (CBS, CRM, ERP, core treasury)', against FY2025 operating expenses +19.4% y/y and administrative costs +13.7% y/y. The bank had previously disclosed digital-infrastructure investment of approximately RON 235m in 2025.
signals.source_name: CEC Bank - Investor Presentation, Year-end results 2025 (PDF, slides 'End-to-end transformation since 2020' and 'Steady performance on higher business volumes and digital expansion')
signals.implies: Two things change versus the baseline. (1) The Temenos programme has moved from 'selected' to 'pilot launched, migration in progress' - the channel and device integration layer (ATM/MFM host interface, card management, POS/acquiring) is being cut over NOW, which is the last moment to position ATM middleware, device-driving software and integration/managed services before the architecture freezes. (2) '>92% of investment linked to IT' means almost nothing is left in the capital budget for hardware while the core migration runs - so a lease / ATM-as-a-Service / managed-service commercial structure will land far better than a capex box sale until the migration completes.
signals.likelihood: High - migration is stated as in progress; full cutover plausibly 2026-27
signals.followup: Probe Temenos/SoftCentric/Tech Mahindra for the phasing and specifically for the self-service integration layer. FIS Quantum and Pluridio are now confirmed treasury vendors - use them to map the integrator bench. Watch Temenos quarterly results for a named CEC go-live.

signals.entity: CEC Bank / all ATM operators in Romania
signals.signal: Senate bill B409/2026 (obliging every payment service provider operating cash-withdrawal ATMs in Romania to let users key in a personalised withdrawal amount, for cardholders of any Romanian-authorised PSP, with fast-cash preset buttons expressly NOT a substitute; RON 50,000-100,000 fines; 90 days to comply from entry into force) has CLEARED ALL FOUR advisory opinions since the last run. New since 30/07/2026: the National Bank of Romania opinion no. G/161/17.08.2026, signed by Governor Mugur Isarescu, states that BNR 'nu se opune' (does not oppose) the proposal, while asking that the text (a) clarify whether the terminal-reconfiguration obligation also binds PSPs authorised in other Member States passporting into Romania under Art.56 of Law 209/2019, (b) resolve that the text covers all 'utilizatori' while the sanction regime is framed only around consumers, and (c) be consulted with the banking system 'in vederea identificarii aspectelor care vizeaza bariere potentiale in implementarea uniforma a caracteristicilor tehnice ale terminalelor de plata'. The Competition Council opinion no. RG 11539/18.08.2026, signed by President Bogdan Chiritoiu, finds nothing contrary to competition or State-aid rules. Both join the favourable CES (14/07/2026) and Legislative Council (679/22.07.2026) opinions. Senate status at 27/08/2026 remains 'inregistrat la Senat pt. dezbatere'; the initiator requested urgent procedure on 24/06/2026 (Procedura de urgenta field still records 'Nu').
signals.source_name: Senate of Romania - legislative file B409/2026, with the BNR opinion (26b409BNR.PDF) and Competition Council opinion (26b409CC.PDF)
signals.implies: The last procedural obstacle that could have killed this bill is gone - the central bank explicitly declined to oppose it. Every ATM in Romania, including CEC's ~1,500 ATMs/MFMs, would need an application/screen-flow change and re-certification inside 90 days, which almost no bank can do in-house. That is a market-wide, deadline-driven ATM software and managed-services engagement. Better still, BNR has formally invited consultation with the banking system on the technical characteristics of terminals - an open door for a vendor with a ready compliance answer to shape the spec now, before the text is fixed.
signals.likelihood: Medium-High - all advisory opinions in and none opposing, but still first-chamber with no vote scheduled
signals.followup: Track the Senate committee report and vote. Engage via the banking association on the BNR-requested technical consultation. Have a market-wide ATM-application compliance offer ready NOW - 90 days from promulgation is not enough lead time to start selling afterwards.

signals.signal: CEC Bank's own tender page (cec.ro/achizitii, checked 27/08/2026) currently lists only ONE procedure - the IT messaging (Info SMS) solution published 25/02/2026 with offers due 13/03/2026. The physical-security risk-analysis procedure of 02/04/2026 that was live at the last run has been removed. No self-service, cash-automation, ATM or POS lot is currently advertised.
signals.implies: Confirms the channel is live and rotated (items are removed once closed), so it must be polled rather than read once. It also confirms no ATM/cash-automation tender is open today - consistent with the investor presentation's '>92% of investments linked to IT', i.e. hardware procurement is being held back while the core-banking migration runs. Get onto the qualified-supplier list before the refresh wave rather than after a notice appears, because the posting-to-deadline window here is roughly two weeks.
signals.likelihood: High that the channel keeps being used; low that a device lot appears in the next quarter
signals.followup: Poll cec.ro/achizitii weekly. Contact Serviciul Independent Achizitii (sia@cec.ro, 021/311.11.19) to be registered as a qualified supplier for self-service, cash automation and security lots - a two-week bid window is not enough time to qualify from cold.

signals.signal: CEC Bank's 2026 Financial Calendar, filed as an FSA Regulation 5/2018 current report to the Financial Supervisory Authority and the Bucharest Stock Exchange on 28/01/2026 (report B-29), sets only two events for the year: publication of the consolidated and standalone financial statements as at 31/12/2025, and publication of 'Interim Consolidated and Standalone Financial Information as at 30.06.2026' on 30/09/2026. A calendar update filed 25/03/2026 moved only the FY2025 publication to 30/04/2026 and left the interim date untouched. Signed by Simona Andrei, Director - Vice President of the Executive Management Board, and Ionut Lianu, CBO.
signals.source_name: CEC Bank - Financial Calendar 2026 (FSA/BVB current report, 28/01/2026) and 2026 Financial calendar update (25/03/2026)
signals.implies: Important scoping fact for this reporting window: CEC Bank does NOT report in the August H1 cluster - its H1-2026 interim information is not due until 30/09/2026. Any August-dated 'CEC H1 results' claim is therefore not from the bank. This also dates the next hard checkpoint for the ROBOR fine provision, the machine-estate figures and the core-banking migration status: 30/09/2026.
signals.likelihood: Certain - it is a filed regulatory calendar
signals.followup: Diary 30/09/2026 and re-run this bank then. The interim statements are the first place a ROBOR provision and any 2026 capex on machines will appear.

signals.signal: RE-VERIFIED TO PRIMARY TIER: CEC Bank's rejection of the Competition Council ROBOR decision, previously carried only as a website statement, is confirmed as a formal current report to the Financial Supervisory Authority and the Bucharest Stock Exchange under FSA Regulation 5/2018, report date 08/06/2026 (registry no. B-191-CBO), headed 'CEC BANK STRONGLY REJECTS THE COMPETITION COUNCIL'S DECISION AND WILL CHALLENGE THE SANCTION IN COURT'. The bank states 'total disagreement', calls the decision 'unjustified, lacking a solid legal foundation and based on wrong interpretations of market mechanisms' and 'categorically reject[s] any accusation of ROBOR rate manipulation'. The filing does NOT state the fine amount and does NOT disclose any provision.
signals.source_name: CEC Bank - Press release regarding the public announcement of the Competition Council (FSA/BVB current report PDF)
signals.implies: The RON 332.98m exposure (c.41% of FY2025 group net profit of RON 815.1m) is now a formally disclosed, contested and unprovisioned item. Combined with the investor presentation's '>92% of investments linked to IT', the 2026-27 procurement posture is clear: no appetite for discretionary hardware capex. Lead every CEC proposition with opex, lease, ATM-as-a-Service and managed-services structures.
signals.likelihood: High - the appeal will run through 2026-27
signals.followup: Check the 30/09/2026 interim statements for whether a provision is booked against the RON 332.98m fine - a booked provision hardens the opex-only stance; no provision means management expects to win.

coverage_notes: Fresh run, no checkpoint existed. Primary-source-first: CEC Bank's own site (press listing, Cash2Card release, Agentia Digitala product page, procurement page, EN and RO investor-relations pages), its FY2025 Investor Presentation PDF (a June-2026 document the previous run never opened, and the single richest new source this run), three FSA/BVB current-report PDFs, and the Senate of Romania legislative file for B409/2026 including the BNR and Competition Council opinion PDFs. The highest-value new technique this run was the branch/ATM locator: cec.ro/sucursale is a Drupal view whose 'localitate' filter accepts an EMPTY value and then returns the ENTIRE national estate server-rendered in one 4.4MB response. De-duplicated on name+address it yields 1,244 ATMs, 256 MFMs, 963 agentii and 48 sucursale. The 963+48 = 1,011 territorial units reconciles EXACTLY with the bank's Pillar 3 figure of 1,011 units at 31/12/2025, which independently validates the de-duplication. This is now a repeatable monthly estate tracker for this bank and the method should be tried on other Drupal-based bank locators. RE-VERIFIED against the baseline: the 1,220 ATM / 264 MFM figures (now 1,244 / 256 on the live locator); the five Digital Agencies (still exactly five, page last modified 31/07/2026 - no rollout decision yet); the 1,011 territorial units (unchanged, confirming the 'we will not close agencies' statement empirically eight months on); the cec.ro/achizitii channel (live, rotated, only one stale procedure open); the ROBOR fine rejection (upgraded from partially-confirmed website statement to a formal FSA/BVB current report). MATERIALLY NEW: Cash2Card (04/08/2026); '24/7 self-service zones (46 units)' and 'cashless units (5)' - the missing conversion denominator; 'Core Banking System (pilot launched, migration in progress)' - first concrete Temenos status; '>92% of investments linked to IT'; FIS Quantum and Pluridio named as treasury vendors; BNR and Competition Council opinions on B409/2026 (17-18/08/2026), both non-opposing; the 30/09/2026 H1-2026 reporting date. GENUINE GAPS: the ATM/MFM OEM is still undisclosed by any party and could not be established this run. The Aurachain fleet-monitoring application's status could not be re-verified - the Aurachain CEC customer story now 404s (see access issues), so whether that layer survived the Temenos programme remains open. No 2026-vintage POS/acquiring terminal count was found. CEC does not report in the August cluster, so there is no H1-2026 disclosure to mine until 30/09/2026 - that is a timing gap, not a search failure.
access_issues: www.cec.ro returns HTTP 403 to the plain fetch tool on every page; worked around by re-requesting the same URLs with a desktop Chrome User-Agent via curl, which returned 200 throughout. Article and product bodies on cec.ro are partly client-rendered - the real content sits after the navigation block and was recovered by stripping tags and reading the tail, with dates cross-checked against the embedded JSON-LD datePublished/dateModified fields. WebSearch was UNAVAILABLE for this entire run: the session's web-search budget (200/200 calls) was already exhausted by earlier banks before this subagent started, so every source here was reached by direct URL fetch rather than by search. This is the main coverage constraint of the run and is the likeliest cause of any missed third-party/press item; it did not affect primary-source coverage, which was done by direct URL. Three CEC PDFs (Financial calendar 2026, the 25/03/2026 calendar update, and the Competition Council current report) are image-only scans - pdfminer returned 1, 1 and 3 characters. No OCR binary (tesseract/ocrmypdf/pdftotext) is installed on this machine, so they were converted to PNG with the macOS 'sips' utility and read visually. That route worked and should be reused for CEC's scanned filings. https://aurachain.ch/customer-stories/cec-bank/ and https://aurachain.ch/customer-stories/ both now return HTTP 404 - the Aurachain CEC customer story that the previous run relied on has been removed from the vendor's site. Logged, not silently dropped. temenos.com/news returned 200 but contains zero CEC Bank mentions. No source was silently dropped.
